title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its plan to improve AI standards, emphasising transparency, accountability, and public safety. It commits to working with stakeholders, setting clear guidelines, and encouraging the ethical use of AI across all sectors.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU Regulation 2024/1689, which establishes harmonised rules for the use and development of artificial intelligence across member states. It also updates several existing regulations and directives to align with the new AI framework.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to protect the fairness, reliability, and integrity of exams. The policy explains measures such as risk assessment, guidance for exam providers, and collaboration with other regulators to manage AI-driven content while safeguarding standards.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted material and evaluates the legal and societal effects. It offers guidance on balancing innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responds to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI in the UK by affirming the need for urgent action and outlining steps to strengthen regulation, investment, and collaboration across industry, academia and public bodies. It stresses the importance of safety, ethics, data sharing and skills development to keep the UK at the forefront of AI innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope and responsibilities of a committee tasked with examining how artificial intelligence affects public standards and governance. It also provides a set of frequently asked questions to help clarify the committee’s objectives and the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of AI, outlining its perspective on how AI should be regulated and managed. The submission emphasizes responsible AI development, transparency, and protecting the public interest.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy outlines how the principles in the AI White Paper will be applied to the regulation of medical products, ensuring safety, efficacy, and transparency in AI‑driven medical technologies. It aims to provide guidance on risk assessment, data governance, and continuous monitoring to protect patients while fostering innovation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence body in AI for its size. It outlines how this will be achieved through investment, collaboration, and high standards for responsible AI use.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI for greater safety, efficiency, and innovation in mobility services. It also details steps to identify and manage the risks associated with implementing AI in transport systems.
